summary: Advance the incremental sync watermark only when every consumed record was stored: extract/hydration failures AND silently-skipped records (scalar deletion tombstones) both hold the watermark. UpsertBatch counts a record stored only after its typed-table projection succeeds, so typed failures also hold the watermark for retry.
reason: Greptile P1 on publish PR #1668: sync --resources deleted (scalar keys) advanced the watermark past records that were never stored, excluding them from all future incremental runs. Extended: the /deleted endpoint returns a category map (collections/items/searches/tags/settings); extractPageItems' known-key strategy kept only the items array, silently dropping deleted collections, searches, and tags. flattenDeletedCategories now flattens every category into storable {key: '<category>/<key>', category} tombstones before upsert. Further extended: stored tombstones are now APPLIED — applyDeletedTombstones hard-deletes the corresponding cached records (typed row, FTS, generic row via store.DeleteResourceByID) so offline commands stop returning deleted records; application errors fail the sync so the watermark never advances past unmirrored tombstones.
validated_outcome: extractFailureTotal > 0 or consumedTotal != totalCount leaves the watermark untouched (SaveSyncProgress preserves the prior watermark); build/tests pass. Live-validated 2026-08-06: sync --resources deleted --resource-param deleted:since=0 stored 695 tombstones (693 items + 2 collections; collections were previously dropped). Tombstone application live-validated: a planted cached record matching a real deleted-item key was removed (tombstones_applied removed=1) with typed and generic rows both gone.
